A post-election slide in chipmakers snowballed as investors bailed from technology shares on speculation that congressional Democrats will clamp down on the artificial-intelligence industry.
In its worst session since March 2020, the Nasdaq 100 sank 6.4%, wiping out $2.3 trillion in value. The S&P 500 fell 4.4%. A key gauge of chip giants tumbled 12%. Qualcomm Inc. and Arm Holdings Plc’s sank on underwhelming outlooks. Apple Inc. raised $7.5 billion from its high-grade bond offering, adding to a flurry of tech issuance. Tesla Inc. and SpaceX slid at least 9%.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Technology stocks plunged the most since 2020 on Thursday as investors exited the sector on concerns over the artificial intelligence trade after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.
The Nasdaq 100 Index sank 6.4%, wiping out $2.3 trillion in market value, the most on record. Tech led a sector-wide rout in the market that sent the S&P 500 Index tumbling 4.4% for its biggest drop since April 2025 when markets were rocked by US President Donald Trump’s Liberation Day tariffs. A gauge of US semiconductor stocks plunged 12% to notch its worst day since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic in March 2020.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Mining companies backed by billions of dollars in support from the Trump administration are facing a new risk: heightened scrutiny after the Democrats’ midterm sweep.
Even before a blue wave overtook Congress, Democratic lawmakers were questioning the methods used for President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the nation’s critical minerals industry. His administration made a flurry of unconventional financing arrangements — including taking equity stakes and issuing stock warrants — to support mining and processing companies in a bid to lessen reliance on China.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Bank of America Corp. is combining its global credit macro, fixed income exchange-traded fund, and high-grade corporate bond trading businesses into a single platform as the Wall Street firm looks to streamline credit trading for clients and boost the liquidity it can offer.
The new structure aligns the bank’s global credit macro and FICC ETF trading businesses with its existing US investment-grade trading and EMEA developed markets flow trading businesses, according to a memo on Thursday from George Brommer and Michail Zekyrgias, co-heads of global credit. It will provide clients with a single, comprehensive platform to manage their credit risk, the memo said.

By Samantha KellyNovember 5, 2026 at 9:07 PM UTCBookmark
Save
Grindr Inc. raised its guidance for the current year and said it expects to meet its 2027 targets about 12 months ahead of schedule, signs the company has been succeeding in its strategy to market itself as more than just a dating app for gay men.
The company now sees $560 million in revenue and $236 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, it said Thursday in a statement. If those new targets are met, Grindr will reach in 2026 what was supposed to be its 2027 adjusted Ebitda goal, following pledges made at the company’s 2024 investor day. That new sales projection represents 93% of the two-year-old revenue target.
